newsitem.title: UK: Copper steady in LME evening, zinc up, nickel down.
newsitem.headline: Copper steady in LME evening, zinc up, nickel down.

text.p: Copper prices held steady during London Metal Exchange (LME) evening inter-office trading as the market remained nervous ahead of next week's July option declarations.
Nickel slumped further on expectations a Canadian strike will end this week-end and zinc surged after a constructive technical close to afternoon trading.

Three months delivery copper held near $2,420 a tonne, where it had ended the afternoon, as the nearby spreads remained tight forcing cash/threes backwardation above $150 a tonne. Further volatile trading is expected next week.

Traders said the further losses in nickel appeared to reflect market expectations that workers at Inco's Sudbury operations would vote for their negotiators reccomendation to agree to the company's latest package.
Three months dipped to near $6,850 a tonne, a loss of around $100 from the afternoon close on the floor of the LME.
Zinc's afternoon burst above chart points at $1,420 and $1,426 a tonne had prompted expectations of renewed fund interest next week and prices continued to edge higher in evening business.
At 1815 GMT three months delivery zinc was trading at $1,433 a tonne, up five dollars from the afternoon.
